title: 八月十五夜赠张功曹
title_en: On the Night of the Fifteenth of the Eighth Month, for Zhang the Revenue Officer
author: 韩愈

text_note.zh: 语料本缺了最后三句“一年明月今宵多，人生由命非由他，有酒不饮奈明何”，这里按通行本补上。语料本的“桮、搥、臯、廻、祗”是旧字形或繁简转换的写法，这里写作“杯、捶、皋、回、只”。
text_note.en: The corpus text is missing the last three lines, which are restored here from the common text. A few old or machine-converted character forms in the corpus (for cup, beat, Gao, back and only) are written in their standard forms here.

readings.zh: “相属”是互相劝酒，读 zhǔ，不读 shǔ。
readings.en: Xiāng zhǔ means to urge each other to drink, so it is read zhǔ, not shǔ.
Háo means animals howling, so it is read háo.
Dà pì means the death penalty, so it is read pì.

readings.zh: “流者还”是被流放的人回来，读 huán。
readings.en: Liú zhě huán means the exiles come back, so it is read huán.

readings.zh: “朝班”是朝廷官员的行列，读 cháo。
readings.en: Cháo bān means the ranks of court officials, so it is read cháo.

readings.zh: “坎轲”同“坎坷”，读 kǎn kě。“轲”单用时读 kē。
readings.en: Kǎn kě is the same word as "bumpy, full of hardship" and is read kǎn kě. On its own this character is read kē.

glosses.zh: 纤云：细细的、薄薄的云。
glosses.en: xiān yún: thin, wispy clouds.

glosses.zh: 四卷：向四面卷走、散开。
glosses.en: sì juǎn: rolled away on all sides.

glosses.zh: 天无河：天上看不见银河，因为月亮太亮了。
glosses.en: tiān wú hé: the Milky Way cannot be seen, because the moon is so bright.

glosses.zh: 月舒波：月光像水波一样铺开。
glosses.en: yuè shū bō: moonlight spreads out like waves.

glosses.zh: 水息：水面平静不动。
glosses.en: shuǐ xī: the water lies still.

glosses.zh: 声影绝：没有一点声音，也没有一点影子在动。
glosses.en: shēng yǐng jué: no sound, no moving shadow.

glosses.zh: 相属：互相劝酒。属，劝人喝酒。
glosses.en: xiāng zhǔ: urging each other to drink. Zhǔ means to offer wine.

glosses.zh: 声酸辞且苦：声音辛酸，歌词也很悲苦。
glosses.en: shēng suān cí qiě kǔ: the voice is bitter and the words are sad.

glosses.zh: 洞庭：洞庭湖，在今湖南。
glosses.en: Dòngtíng: Dongting Lake, in today's Hunan.

glosses.zh: 九疑：九疑山，在今湖南南部，传说舜葬在这里。
glosses.en: Jiǔyí: the Jiuyi Mountains in southern Hunan, where the sage king Shun is said to be buried.

glosses.zh: 蛟龙：传说中能发洪水的龙。
glosses.en: jiāo lóng: a dragon of legend that brings floods.

glosses.zh: 猩鼯：猩猩和鼯鼠。鼯鼠是一种能在树间滑翔的松鼠。
glosses.en: xīng wú: apes and flying squirrels. A flying squirrel glides from tree to tree.

glosses.zh: 十生九死：十个人里九个会死，说路途非常危险。
glosses.en: shí shēng jiǔ sǐ: of ten who go, nine die; the journey is deadly.

glosses.zh: 官所：做官的地方。
glosses.en: guān suǒ: the post where one serves as an official.

glosses.zh: 如藏逃：像逃犯一样躲藏着。
glosses.en: rú cáng táo: hiding like a runaway.

glosses.zh: 食畏药：吃饭怕被人下毒。药，毒药。
glosses.en: shí wèi yào: afraid of poison in the food. Yào here means poison.

glosses.zh: 海气湿蛰：南方靠海，潮湿的空气里藏着各种虫子。蛰，藏着的虫。
glosses.en: hǎi qì shī zhé: near the sea, the damp air is full of hidden insects and creatures. Zhé means creatures in hiding.

glosses.zh: 熏腥臊：散发出腥臭难闻的气味。
glosses.en: xūn xīng sāo: giving off a fishy, foul smell.

glosses.zh: 昨者：前些日子。
glosses.en: zuó zhě: the other day.

glosses.zh: 捶大鼓：敲大鼓。古代宣布大赦时要敲鼓。
glosses.en: chuí dà gǔ: beating the great drum, as was done when a general pardon was announced.

glosses.zh: 嗣皇继圣：新皇帝继承了皇位。嗣皇，继位的皇帝，这里指唐顺宗。
glosses.en: sì huáng jì shèng: the new emperor took the throne. Sì huáng means the heir who became emperor, here Emperor Shunzong.

glosses.zh: 登夔皋：任用像夔和皋陶那样的贤臣。夔和皋陶是传说中舜时的两位好大臣。
glosses.en: dēng Kuí Gāo: raising up wise ministers like Kui and Gao Yao, two good ministers of the sage king Shun in legend.

glosses.zh: 赦书：皇帝宣布赦免罪人的文书。
glosses.en: shè shū: the emperor's decree of pardon.

glosses.zh: 罪从大辟：从死罪往下的各种罪。大辟，死刑。
glosses.en: zuì cóng dà pì: every crime from the death penalty on down. Dà pì means death penalty.

glosses.zh: 除死：免去死罪。
glosses.en: chú sǐ: spared from death.

glosses.zh: 迁者：被贬到外地的官员。
glosses.en: qiān zhě: officials sent away to posts far from the capital as punishment.

glosses.zh: 流者：被流放的人。
glosses.en: liú zhě: people sent into exile.

glosses.zh: 涤瑕荡垢：洗去污点和脏东西，比喻清除过去的错误。
glosses.en: dí xiá dàng gòu: washing away stains and dirt, meaning clearing old wrongs.

glosses.zh: 清朝班：让朝廷的官员队伍变得清明。
glosses.en: qīng cháo bān: making the ranks of court officials clean and fair.

glosses.zh: 州家申名：州里的长官把我们的名字报上去，请求让我们回京。
glosses.en: zhōu jiā shēn míng: the prefect sent up our names, asking that we be called back.

glosses.zh: 使家抑：上面的观察使把这件事压了下来。
glosses.en: shǐ jiā yì: the regional inspector above him held it back.

glosses.zh: 坎轲：同“坎坷”，道路不平，比喻命运不顺。
glosses.en: kǎn kě: bumpy, full of hardship; a hard road in life.

glosses.zh: 荆蛮：指荆州一带，就是江陵（今湖北荆州）。古时中原人这样称呼南方。
glosses.en: Jīng mán: the Jingzhou area, meaning Jiangling (today's Jingzhou in Hubei). Old northerners called the south by this name.

glosses.zh: 判司：州府里管具体事务的小官。
glosses.en: pàn sī: a low official handling daily business in a prefecture.

glosses.zh: 不堪说：说起来都难受。
glosses.en: bù kān shuō: too painful to talk about.

glosses.zh: 捶楚：用棍子、荆条打人。小官犯错会被上司责打。
glosses.en: chuí chǔ: beating with rods. A low official could be beaten by his superiors.

glosses.zh: 辈流：同一批被贬的人。
glosses.en: bèi liú: others exiled at the same time.

glosses.zh: 上道：上路回京城了。
glosses.en: shàng dào: set out on the road back to the capital.

glosses.zh: 天路：去京城、去朝廷的路。
glosses.en: tiān lù: the road to the capital and the court.

glosses.zh: 追攀：追上去，攀上去。
glosses.en: zhuī pān: to catch up and climb up.

glosses.zh: 殊科：不一样。科，类别。
glosses.en: shū kē: different. Kē means a kind or class.

glosses.zh: 今宵多：今天晚上的月亮最圆最亮。
glosses.en: jīn xiāo duō: tonight the moon is at its fullest and brightest.

glosses.zh: 奈明何：对得起这明月吗？意思是辜负了明月。
glosses.en: nài míng hé: what about this bright moon? That is, we would let the moon down.

translation.zh: 细细的云向四面散开，天上看不见银河，
translation.en: Thin clouds roll away on all sides; the Milky Way cannot be seen.

translation.zh: 清风吹过天空，月光像水波一样铺开。
translation.en: A clear wind sweeps the sky, and moonlight spreads like waves.

translation.zh: 沙滩平平，水面静静，没有声音，也没有影子，
translation.en: The sand is flat, the water still, no sound, no moving shadow.

translation.zh: 我端起一杯酒劝你喝，你该唱首歌。
translation.en: I raise a cup to you; now you should sing.

translation.zh: 你的歌声辛酸，歌词悲苦，
translation.en: Your voice is bitter and your words are sad;

translation.zh: 我听不完就泪如雨下。
translation.en: before the song is done my tears fall like rain.

translation.zh: （你唱道：）“洞庭湖水连着天，九疑山高高耸立，
translation.en: (You sing:) "Dongting Lake meets the sky, the Jiuyi Mountains stand high,

translation.zh: 蛟龙在水里出没，猩猩和鼯鼠在哀叫。
translation.en: dragons rise and sink in the water, apes and flying squirrels howl.

translation.zh: 九死一生才到了做官的地方，
translation.en: We barely lived to reach our posts,

translation.zh: 住在偏僻的地方默默无声，像逃犯一样躲藏。
translation.en: and lived there silent and hidden, like runaways.

translation.zh: 下床怕踩到蛇，吃饭怕被下毒，
translation.en: Getting out of bed we feared snakes; eating, we feared poison;

translation.zh: 海边潮湿的空气里藏着虫子，又腥又臭。
translation.en: the damp sea air was full of creatures and foul smells.

translation.zh: 前些日子，州衙门前敲起了大鼓，
translation.en: The other day the great drum was beaten before the prefecture:

translation.zh: 新皇帝登基，要任用贤良的大臣。
translation.en: a new emperor had taken the throne and would raise up wise ministers.

translation.zh: 赦免的文书一天就传了上万里，
translation.en: The pardon traveled ten thousand li in a day;

translation.zh: 从死罪往下，所有犯人都免了死。
translation.en: everyone, even those condemned to die, was spared.

translation.zh: 贬官被召回，流放的人也能回家，
translation.en: Demoted officials were called back and exiles returned,

translation.zh: 洗去过去的污点，让朝廷变得清明。
translation.en: old stains were washed away and the court made clean.

translation.zh: 州里的长官把我们的名字报上去，上面的观察使却压了下来，
translation.en: Our prefect sent up our names, but the inspector above held them back;

translation.zh: 命运不顺，我们只能调到荆蛮之地。
translation.en: our luck was bad, and we were only moved to the land of Jing.

translation.zh: 当个判司这样的小官，苦处说也说不完，
translation.en: A low post like pàn sī is too painful to speak of;

translation.zh: 免不了在尘土里挨上司的板子。
translation.en: we cannot escape being beaten in the dust.

translation.zh: 和我们一起被贬的人，很多都已上路回京了，
translation.en: Many exiled with us are already on the road back,

translation.zh: 可通往朝廷的路又暗又险，我们追也追不上。”
translation.en: but the road to the court is dark and steep, and we cannot catch up."

translation.zh: 你先别唱了，听我唱一首，
translation.en: Stop your song for now and listen to mine;

translation.zh: 我的歌和你的不一样。
translation.en: my song today is not like yours.

translation.zh: 一年里的明月，今晚最圆最亮，
translation.en: Of all the year's bright moons, tonight's is the fullest;

translation.zh: 人生由命运决定，不是由别的什么，
translation.en: life is ruled by fate, and nothing else;

translation.zh: 有酒不喝，怎么对得起这明月呢？
translation.en: if we have wine and do not drink, how can we face this bright moon?

background.zh: 贞元十九年（803年），韩愈和张署都在朝廷做监察御史，因为上书说了实话，被贬到南方：韩愈去了阳山（今属广东），张署去了临武（今属湖南）。805年新皇帝唐顺宗即位，大赦天下。他们在郴州（今属湖南）等待新的任命，结果只被调到江陵府做小官：韩愈当法曹参军，张署当功曹参军。这一年中秋夜，两人在郴州喝酒赏月，韩愈写了这首诗送给张署。
background.en: In 803 Han Yu and Zhang Shu were both censors at court. Because they spoke honestly in a report to the throne, they were sent away to the south: Han Yu to Yangshan (in today's Guangdong) and Zhang Shu to Linwu (in today's Hunan). In 805 a new emperor, Shunzong, took the throne and pardoned the whole land. The two waited in Chenzhou (in today's Hunan) for new posts, but were only moved to low jobs in Jiangling: Han Yu as a law officer and Zhang Shu as a revenue officer. On the Mid-Autumn night that year, they drank and watched the moon in Chenzhou, and Han Yu wrote this poem for Zhang Shu.

author_note.zh: 韩愈（768—824），字退之，唐代文学家、思想家，“唐宋八大家”之首。他为人正直，敢说真话，一生几次被贬。他的诗喜欢用奇特的字句，气势很大。这首诗借朋友的歌说出两人的苦，最后用自己的歌劝朋友想开一点。
author_note.en: Han Yu (768–824), also called Tuizhi, was a Tang writer and thinker, first of the Eight Great Prose Masters of Tang and Song. He was upright and dared to speak the truth, and he was sent away from the court several times. His poems like bold, unusual words and have great force. Here he lets his friend's song tell of their suffering, and then uses his own song to cheer his friend up.

appreciation.zh: 诗一开头特别安静：云散了，风清了，月光像水一样铺开，四周一点声音也没有。在这样的月夜，两个被贬的朋友对坐喝酒。接着，大半首诗都是张署的歌：路上有湖、有高山、有蛟龙和怪兽；到了地方，怕蛇、怕毒、怕潮湿；好不容易遇上大赦，却又被人压住，只换了个小官。这些苦，让人听了都要掉泪。最后韩愈说：你别唱了，听我的。今晚月亮最圆，命运不由人，有酒就喝吧。话说得很洒脱，可心里其实也很苦。
appreciation.en: The poem opens in deep quiet. The clouds have gone, the wind is clear, moonlight spreads like water, and there is no sound at all. On such a night, two exiled friends sit drinking. Then most of the poem is Zhang Shu's song. On the road there were lakes, high mountains, dragons and strange beasts. At their posts they feared snakes, poison and damp. At last a pardon came, but someone blocked them, and they got only small new jobs. Hearing these troubles would make anyone cry. Finally Han Yu says: stop your song and hear mine. Tonight the moon is fullest, fate is not in our hands, so if there is wine, let us drink. He sounds carefree, but inside he is hurting too.
